candidates.text: He steps out onto the craggy path beneath the lamp room, the wind whipping the sea‑spray into brittle crystals around him, and kneels at the mouth of the cliff where the stone wall meets the jagged edge. A narrow slab of timber frames a doorway that hadn’t been there in daylight—or even the last night’s lantern light—so he brushes away a patch of moss‑clinging lichen, feeling the cold iron knob embedded in the rough mortar; when he turns it, the door sighs open with a low creak, revealing a dimly lit chamber lined with crumbling stone shelves, a single candle guttering, and a map pinned to the far wall marked with an X that seemed to point toward the very heart of the cliffs.

The keeper descended the winding stone path, the wind whipping his coat against his face as he reached the shadowed alcove beneath the lamp room. With a slow, careful tug on the rusted iron handle—its hinges groaning despite its age—the solid wood panel swung inward, revealing a narrow passage lit by a faint, amber glow that did not match any lantern or beacon above. A chill brushed his spine when he stepped inside, and the scent of salt‑worn timber mingled with something older, almost metallic, suggesting that beyond this hidden doorway lay more than just another corridor of fog and gulls’ cries.

He eased himself down the winding stone stair, the wind howling through the cracks like a restless beast, until he reached the edge of the cliff’s lip and stared into the dark mouth of the fissure where the door lay concealed among the rotting lichen. With trembling fingers he pushed aside a veil of sea‑sprayed moss, and there, half swallowed by jagged rock, stood a narrow wooden doorway whose frame was etched with a faded symbol—a stylized compass rose flanked by two spiraling shells—that he had never once seen on any chart. When he turned the stubborn brass lock, the hinges sang and the door swung inward, releasing a wave of cool, damp air that carried the scent of salt and age; inside, the chamber was illuminated only by flickering candles and the ghostly glow of a broken lantern, and beside them lay rows of weather‑worn maps, a cracked mirror reflecting a distant beam fading out the window, and a single, dust‑caked journal whose pages whispered promises of a forgotten treasure hidden below the sea’s own ribs.

instruction: Answer the brief as you normally would.

task.brief: A lighthouse keeper finds a door in the cliff below the lamp room that was not there yesterday. Write the next paragraph.
good_idea_qualities: the door implies a consequence the keeper must act on
the paragraph keeps the sea and the lamp in view
something is at stake for the keeper personally
task.reference_text: The keeper set the oil can down and counted the door twice, the way he counted ships. It was blue, salt-blistered, and hinged on the seaward side, which meant whoever built it had worked from the water.
